children: Orrick, Herrington & Sutcliffe said on Tuesday that it has hired two new executives who will drive the law firm’s technology and finance functions at a time when artificial intelligence is reshaping legal industry priorities.

The San Francisco-founded firm has hired Padma Elmgart as chief technology officer from KKR subsidiary Global Atlantic Financial Group, and Chris Davis as chief financial officer from Paul Hastings. Both executives are based in New York.

Elmgart joined Global Atlantic as chief technology officer in 2019 from Deutsche Bank, and previously worked at other banks including Barclays. She currently serves on the board of directors of HSBC North America and is vice chair of nonprofit Streetwise Partners.

“Legal services is at a particularly interesting moment because the capabilities of technology are changing so rapidly,” particularly around generative AI and large language models, Elmgart told Reuters. She said her experience working in financial services during a period of technological transformation will help guide her work at the law firm.

Elmgart will lead Orrick’s global technology organization and strategy and will work with others at the firm to use technology, data and AI to “create differentiated value for clients and transform how the firm operates,” the firm said.
She starts at the firm on September 21. Global Atlantic did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Competition to successfully integrate AI has become a key driver in law firm hiring over the past year, with major firms bringing on a spate of new executives and technical specialists.

Law firm expenses have increased this year, driven by investments in technology, including AI, according to data from the Thomson Reuters Institute. The Thomson Reuters Institute and Reuters share the same parent company.

Davis, the firm’s new finance chief who started on Monday, was most recently chief operating officer at rival Paul Hastings and previously worked at Goodwin Procter. Paul Hastings did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Davis told Reuters he plans to focus on innovation in his new role.
